title: Internet of Things and Smart Cities

pages.c21-p01: Explain what the Internet of Things is and describe the parts of an IoT system
pages.c21-p02: Describe common sensors and actuators and how they form an input-process-output system
pages.c21-p03: Evaluate the benefits and risks of smart home devices
pages.c21-p04: Describe how smart cities use IoT data to improve services, and discuss the concerns
pages.c21-p05: Explain why IoT devices are often insecure and describe how laws and users can make them safer
pages.c21-p06: Design an IoT solution to a real problem, considering users, data, security and sustainability

q.q: What is the Internet of Things?
o: Everyday objects connected to the internet

q.q: Which is an IoT device?
What is an embedded system?
o: A small computer built into a device to do one job

Which part of an IoT system lets people see data and send commands?
Which connection might an IoT device use?
Roughly how many IoT devices are there worldwide?
Which is an example of IoT in farming?
Which is an example of IoT in health?
Can you usually install other apps on an embedded system?
o: No: it's built for one job

q.q: What does a sensor do?
o: Measures something and turns it into data

q.q: What does an actuator do?
Which is a sensor?
Which is an actuator?
Which sensor detects movement of people?
Which sensor measures distance, e.g. how full a bin is?
Which sensor would a livestock tracker use?
In "IF moisture < 30% THEN pump on", which part is the process?
What is a feedback loop?
o: When output affects the next input so the system adjusts

q.q: Which uses a feedback loop?
o: A thermostat keeping a room at 20 °C

q.q: Which BBC micro:bit feature is a sensor?
An automatic streetlight uses which sensor?
What is a smart home?
o: A home with devices controlled remotely or automatically

q.q: Which is a voice assistant?
How can smart heating save energy?
o: Heating only when people are home or rooms are in use

q.q: Which is a privacy risk of smart home devices?
o: Data about your routines is collected and sent to companies
q.why: Data collection is a privacy issue.

q.q: What might happen if a smart device company shuts down?
How can smart home devices help older people?
o: Reminders and alerts help them live independently

q.q: What is interoperability?
o: Using a device in the bath
Devices from different makers working together

q.q: What is Matter?
o: A smart home standard to help devices from different brands work together

q.q: What should you check before buying a smart device?
o: How long it gets security updates and what data it collects

q.q: Why is local control useful in smart devices?
o: They can keep working if the internet goes down

q.q: Who should you tell if someone uses smart devices to frighten or track you?
q.why: Get help from people you trust.

q.q: What is a smart city?
o: A city using sensors and data to run services better

q.q: How do smart bins help councils?
o: Lorries only collect bins that are full

q.q: How can smart traffic lights help?
What do air-quality sensors show a city?
What is a digital twin?
o: A virtual model of a real place updated with live data

q.q: Why might a council publish open data?
o: So others can use it to build apps and spot problems

q.q: What is surveillance?
q.why: A key concern in smart cities.

q.q: Which is a concern about smart cities?
o: Who owns and controls the data

q.q: Why might smart city services leave some people out?
o: Some people don't have smartphones or internet

q.q: Which smart solution reduces energy used by streetlights?
o: LEDs that dim when nobody's around

q.q: Real-time bus tracking helps passengers by...
o: showing when the next bus will arrive

q.q: Which is a smart solution for flooding?
o: Water-level sensors that trigger early warnings

q.q: Why are default passwords dangerous?
o: They're the same on many devices and published online

q.q: What is firmware?
o: The software built into a device

q.q: Why are cheap IoT devices often insecure?
o: They may get no security updates and have weak passwords

q.q: What is a botnet?
o: A network of hijacked devices controlled by criminals

q.q: Which botnet took over IoT devices using default passwords in 2016?
What did the Mirai botnet do with hijacked devices?
o: Flooded an internet company with traffic, taking websites offline

q.q: What does DDoS stand for?
q.why: It floods a target with traffic.

q.q: Would an owner usually know their device was in a botnet?
What do the UK PSTI rules ban?
o: Universal default passwords on new smart devices
q.why: Each device needs a unique password.

q.q: Since when have the UK PSTI rules applied?
q.why: They came into force in April 2024.

q.q: What must device makers tell customers under PSTI?
o: How long the device will receive security updates

q.q: What else must makers provide under PSTI?
o: A way to report security problems

q.q: Which habit protects a smart device?
o: Changing the default password and installing updates

q.q: Why put smart devices on a separate guest network?
o: So a hacked device can't easily reach your laptops and phones

q.q: What should IoT design start with?
o: A real problem and its users

q.q: What is a user story?
What is privacy by design?
o: Building privacy in from the start
Adding a privacy page at the end

q.q: Which choice follows privacy by design for counting library visitors?
o: Use a motion counter instead of a camera
q.why: Don't collect personal data you don't need.

q.q: What is security by design?
o: Building security in from the start
Adding a lock to the box

q.q: Which design choice is more sustainable?
o: A long-lasting, repairable device with low power use
A device with a disposable battery
A device that must be replaced yearly
A device that can't be opened

q.q: What is a prototype?
o: An early working model used to test ideas

q.q: Why test a prototype with real users?
o: To find problems and improve it before building the final version

q.q: What should you decide about data in an IoT design?
o: What's collected, how often, where it's stored and who sees it
Only the colour of the graph

q.q: Which power source suits a remote garden sensor?
Which is a good IF ... THEN rule for a school garden?
o: IF dry THEN switch off sensor
IF soil moisture < 30% AND not raining THEN water
q.why: It saves water and helps plants.

q.q: Why might a non-tech solution sometimes be better?
o: It can be simpler, cheaper and more reliable
q.why: Use tech only when it helps.

q.q: Which IoT device is most likely to need a camera?
Which part of a smart thermostat is the actuator?
o: The switch that turns the boiler on and off

q.q: A smart fridge orders milk when it runs low. Which sensor might it use?
q.why: It detects how much is left.

q.q: Which is a fair argument FOR smart cities?
o: They can reduce pollution and save public money

q.q: Which is a fair argument AGAINST smart cities?
o: They could enable too much surveillance
They help buses run on time

Attackers could exploit known weaknesses to watch or hijack it

q.q: Which is the BEST description of the IoT?
o: Billions of everyday objects that sense, share data and act

q.q: Why is the IoT growing so fast?
o: Sensors, chips and connections have become cheap and small

the last country to do so
